note: Re-measurement of UpdateItem's size limits after the 2026-11-21 ground-truth sweep found all 33 regions storing updates the statement-sized rule refused. Each figure was bisected against a fresh on-demand table with string attributes only, and the accepted side read back where noted. `max` is the largest size accepted; one more is refused with `refusal`. Item sizes count names plus values, key included. Two runs from one process on 2026-11-21: run 1 sizes the finished item on each update surface, run 2 sizes what the SET clauses write while the stored item stays tiny (each target already holds a value and if_not_exists keeps it).

what.p1_setShortKey: SET b = :pad at a 2-3 byte key; max is the finished item size
what.p1_readBack: stored size of the item accepted at p1's max
what.p2_setLongKey: the same at a 100-byte key value
what.p3_ifNotExistsValue: SET c = if_not_exists(c, :v) on an item holding c; max is the length of :v
what.p4_overWithFailingCondition: p3 one byte over, with ConditionExpression attribute_exists(nope)
what.p5_padCeilingWithUnusedValue_N: SET b = :p, c = if_not_exists(c, :v) with :v of N bytes on an item holding c; max is the length of :p
what.p6_listIndex: SET l[0] = :p on an item holding a one-element list; max is the length of :p
what.p7_partiql: PartiQL UPDATE SET b = ?; max is the finished item size
what.p7_transact: TransactWriteItems Update SET b = :p; max is the finished item size
what.p8_withUntouched: SET b = :p beside a 1,000-byte untouched attribute; max is the finished item size
